summary: Docked ThinkPad intermittently enters S3 suspend loop after USB-C controller firmware rollout
description:
Issue summary: Several docked corporate ThinkPads have started entering a suspend/resume loop (S3) after the March USB-C controller firmware (FW v1.4.3) was rolled out via SCCM. Impact: Users lose active sessions when laptops are docked and idle; some sessions disconnect from peripheral monitors and RDP sessions drop. Scope: We've received 7 reports across the NYC office in the last 24h; reproducer machines are all on the recent firmware version. Environment: Corporate-managed Windows 11 22H2 images, managed via SCCM; docking hardware: Lenovo USB-C Dock Gen 2, firmware 3.2.0; USB-C controller firmware deployed to laptop models listed in affected_models.

Expected behavior: Docked laptops remain on on AC power; lid closed/sleep behavior follows configured power plan (do not suspend while docked).

Observed behavior: Machines enter S3 unexpectedly when left idle (Kernel-Power Event ID 42 recorded). When docked and lid closed, device sometimes suspends after 2-5 minutes, then wakes immediately and repeats. Affected users report monitors flicker, peripheral reconnection events in Device Manager, and interrupted work.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start with a ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 10 on Windows 11 22H2, SCCM client confirming USB-C controller FW v1.4.3 and Dock firmware 3.2.0.
2) Dock via Lenovo USB-C Dock Gen 2 and close lid (expect no suspend if power plan configured to 'Do nothing' when lid closed).
3) Leave idle for 10 minutes.
4) Observe system entering sleep (Event ID 42) and immediate resume; repeat cycle every few minutes.
5) Check Event Viewer > System for Kernel-Power, USB hub disconnect/attach events, and Application logs for driver errors.
investigation_notes:
- Initial reports started after SCCM rollout of USB-C controller FW v1.4.3 on 2026-03-09 (deployment group: Corp-Laptops).
- Reproduced on two lab units with the same firmware and dock firmware 3.2.0. Not reproducible when laptops are undocked.
- Event Viewer shows repeated Kernel-Power Event ID 42: 'The system is entering sleep.' Timestamps align with USB hub power state changes.
- Device Manager shows 'USB Composite Device' re-enumeration around suspend/resume times.
- Tested rollback to previous USB-C controller firmware (v1.3.9) on one unit: suspend loop stopped within 15 minutes of rollback.
- Hypothesis: New USB-C controller firmware is intermittently asserting a docking/de-asserting signal (ACPI or USB hub power change) which the OS interprets as lid/AC change and triggers configured sleep policy.
- Cross-checked SCCM deployment logs: ~85% of target fleet received v1.4.3 in the last 36 hours.
- Correlated Slack thread: #internal-support/seq: message thread 2026-03-09 16:12 indicates IT pushed v1.4.3 as 'security/compat update'.
- No kernel BSODs or WHEA events found; issue limited to power state transitions.
workaround:
1) Temporary mitigation: Roll back USB-C controller firmware to v1.3.9 via SCCM package 'usb-c-fw-rollback-2026-03-11' for affected serials.
2) Alternate mitigation for users: In Power Options -> Choose what closing the lid does -> set 'When plugged in' to 'Do nothing' and disable 'Allow hybrid sleep'. Note: this is a partial workaround and may not prevent loops if the root signal is a peripheral re-enumeration.
3) As an additional short-term setting, disable 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' for USB Root Hubs is likely to reduce spurious power events.
next_steps:
- Authorize SCCM rollback for impacted deployment group (Corp-Laptops-us-east) and schedule rollout during maintenance window. (Owner: IT Imaging)
- Collect full driver and FW dump from one repro unit (serial + SCCM logs). (Owner: Ethan Morales)
- Open escalation with Lenovo hardware support and include Kernel-Power traces and USB power state logs. (Owner: Maya Chen)
- Update confluence runbook with checklist for rollback and verification steps.
- Add telemetry: enable verbose USB hub logging via registry on a small test cohort to capture the exact ACPI/PNP event sequence.
- Plan: If Lenovo confirms FW regression, coordinate a signed fix and blocked SCCM deployment until vendor patch is validated.
